subject: Electrical Engineering
title: RC Time Constants
description: A micro-lesson that makes RC Time Constants usable.

hook.text: A capacitor doesn't charge instantly. It fills up along a smooth exponential curve.

buildup.text: The time constant τ equals R times C. It sets how fast the cap charges or discharges.

discovery.text: After one τ, the capacitor reaches 63% of full charge. After five τ, it's 99% full.

twist.text: This same curve describes camera flash timing, touch screen response, and audio filters.

climax.text: RC circuits are everywhere — from debouncing buttons to shaping radio signals.

punchline.text: R times C tells you how fast a circuit responds.

quiz.question: What percentage of full charge does a capacitor reach after one time constant?
